countersHowMeasured.nonWhitespaceGlyphsOutsideMeasuredWriteB: MEASURED INDEPENDENTLY AND NOT COPIED, because the builder hardcodes this key. My value is 0 on canonical and 0 on boundary, and here is why it is a real zero rather than a repeated one. Every delivered page content stream is 'q' + the source page's own content + a tail, and those 7 tails carry ZERO text-showing operators, so no glyph is drawn directly on the page. Every added glyph therefore lives inside a FlatWidget Form XObject, which PDF clips to its own /BBox. I enumerated all 144 placements per fixture, computed each one's placed rectangle from its CTM and /Matrix and /BBox, and found 16 glyph-bearing placements carrying 218 non-whitespace glyphs on canonical and 461 on boundary, every one of them contained in a declared write box to within 0.01 pt, and 0 placements beyond the 612x792 MediaBox. So the true value is 0 - and it is the wrong instrument for this packet's actual defect, which is a stroke and not a glyph.

CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP.finding:
Every WRITTEN text widget on both Colorado forms is delivered as a closed stroked black RECTANGLE where the pinned source prints a single writing RULE. Proved three independent ways. (1) On the page: at 600 dpi the source shows 'Colorado County: ______', 'Date of Birth: ______', 'Mailing Address: ______', 'City, State, & Zip: ______', 'Phone: ______' and 'Email: ______' as ruled lines; the delivered packet shows each value inside a four-sided box. (2) In the source bytes: the County widget's /AP /N is exactly '0 G
0 0.5 m
193.636 0.5 l
s
' - one bottom rule - and the widget declares /BS /S /U (underline style, ISO 32000-1 Table 168) with /BS /W 1 and /MK /BC [0 0 0]. All 16 written widgets declare /BS /S /U and all 16 ship a rule-only /AP /N. (3) In the delivered bytes: the flattened appearance for County is '0 0 0 RG 1 w [] 0 d 1 0 0 1 0.5 0.5 cm 0 0 m 0 11.24 l 192.636 11.24 l 192.636 0 l h S' - a closepath-stroke of all four sides. This is pdf-lib's unconditional rectangle synthesised from /MK /BC, drawn in place of the declared underline. Magnitude measured at 600 dpi as added dark pixels in the 2 pt bands along the three sides the source does not print: 277,805 per canonical fixture and 277,809 per boundary fixture, i.e. 58.8% of all added ink in the canonical packet (472,566 added dark pixels over pages 1, 5 and 6) is a frame the Colorado Judicial Department does not print. 9 widgets on JDF-641 (8 on packet page 1, 1 on packet page 5) and 7 on JDF-642 packet page 6. The shared module already carries the exact remedy - honorWidgetBorderStyle in scripts/rcap-official-forms/rcap-active-content.mjs, whose own comment reads 'a court's writing rule delivered as a boxed field is wrong wherever it occurs' - and scripts/build-census-v1-co_multiple_conviction_seal-set.mjs does not pass it. This lane repaired nothing and names the remedy without applying it. || I separately re-measured the two things the record says about this obligation on this family and both hold. (a) VF08's recorded CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP FAIL - field 11.1 on JDF-641 page 5, an /AP /BBox 396 pt wide against a /Rect 392.4 pt wide - DOES NOT REPRODUCE at this base. I read the delivered placement matrices myself: 11.1 is placed at exactly [147.6 488.65 540 553.33], overhang 0.0 pt on all four sides, and every one of the 14 placements on packet page 5 sits inside its own source /Rect to within 0.001 pt. SELF_HELP_STOP.finding: Present and specific. participant-instructions.md closes with 'What this packet is not': 'This is a prepared set of official Colorado Judicial Department forms. It is not legal advice, it is not filed for you, and it does not decide whether your convictions can be sealed.' It then points the participant at page 3 of JDF 641, which prints the list of convictions that are not eligible, and tells them to read it against their own record before signing. The eligibility election at section 5 is left unmade and disclosed as the participant's, with the reason that the packet does not decide eligibility. Nothing in the guide asserts eligibility, a deadline, a clerk's practice or an outcome.

FILING_DESTINATION.finding: Stated, and stated by refusal where the platform holds nothing. The guide's 'Where you file this' names the clerk of the Colorado court that handled the convictions - the District or County Court in the county already filled in on both forms - and then refuses the street address in as many words: 'The Colorado Judicial Department publishes each courthouse's address; this packet does not state one, because the platform holds no court directory and an unsourced address in a filing instruction is worse than none.' The Court Address field is left blank on both forms and disclosed to the participant on both. No address is fabricated. The county written into both captions is matter.county = Denver, the same value on both forms.

SERVICE.finding: Instructed, and correctly sequenced. Step 5 of 'What you must do before you file' reads 'Serve a copy on the prosecuting attorney, then complete the certificate of service in section 9 - the date, the method and who you sent it to. After you have served, not before.' The four certificate-of-service fields (CoS_Date, CoS_Name, CoS_Address, CoS_Other) and the service-method selection GroupCoS are all left blank; I confirmed by raster that none of them carries ink. The guide states no service deadline and no service rule beyond what the form itself prints, which is the correct refusal for a rule no bound source establishes.

ARTIFACTS.finding: This is the obligation MASTER_QUEUE records as failed on this family and it is NOT discharged at this base. Two independent grounds. (1) The delivered artifact carries 16 flattened widget appearances per fixture that match NO stream either pinned source ships - they are pdf-lib's own regenerated appearances, each drawing a synthesized closepath rectangle plus the written value, in place of a source /AP /N that draws one rule (full proof under CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP). VF90's byte-accounting sweep, which is what recorded this obligation, counts only STROKE-ONLY appearances, so by construction it cannot see a synthesized rectangle drawn in the same stream as a written value; FIX135's post-repair figure of '134 stroke-only flattened appearances, 134 matched byte-identically, 0 unmatched' is true within that subset and silent about these 16. (2) reports/actual-writes.json publishes nonWhitespaceGlyphsOutsideMeasuredWriteBoxes as 0 on all four documents, and scripts/build-census-v1-co_multiple_conviction_seal-set.mjs line 904 emits that key as a LITERAL 0 that no code path computes, while line 713 gates the visualDefects counter on that same literal - so this family's visualDefects counter cannot become non-zero however the page looks. That is the recorded defect class 'a-published-zero-where-a-measurement-existed' plus 'a-geometry-counter-with-no-teeth', present together, in an artifact this family ships. I measured the true value myself and it is 0 (see countersHowMeasured), so the published number is right by coincidence of these bytes and not because anything measured it. Everything else about the artifact set is in order: 7 pages in both fixtures by pdfinfo, digests recompute, 14 raster page PNGs present, and reports/ carries actual-writes, blanks-left-for-the-participant, caption-evidence, completeness-counters, independent-visual-review and rendered-artifacts.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.finding: Measured, and the packet's treatment is a refusal rather than a gap. The guide states: 'Ask the clerk what fee applies. It is not established in any source this packet holds, so it is not stated here.' It then states the one fee a bound source does establish, and attributes it: 'The Colorado Bureau of Investigation charges its own fee. JDF 642 says so on its face, in a note addressed to you.' I confirmed that note is printed on JDF 642. No filing fee, no waiver eligibility rule and no waiver deadline is invented anywhere in the packet. No fee-waiver instrument is a declared component of this packet set - the manifest carries exactly two components, both official_pdf_fill - so none is missing. Recorded and not reconciled: the same manifest's participantActionRequired carries an apply_fee_waiver entry whose own description is 'The source review does not address a fee waiver', and a pay_fee and a notarize entry both marked requirement 'required' whose descriptions read 'The source review does not state a filing fee for this motion' and 'The source review does not state a notarization requirement'. Those three manifest rows contradict themselves; the packet resolves each by refusing to state what no source establishes, which is the correct direction, and the guide mentions no notarization at all.
